ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a Ryde reviewer: check the 23:03–23:14 off-route segment against the driver's statement (F11) that he drove Hougang Avenue 3 rather than the agreed Upper Paya Lebar Road, and only then decide the RD-2 refund; no flag_account and no auto-refund on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Both sides agree, and the trace confirms, that this is a metered RydeTAXI trip with one off-route segment: 23:03–23:14, 7.28 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.25 km, adding 5.04 km [F3][F7]. Under RD-1 that segment is a deviation and, since the RD-4 screen marks no qualifying incident [F15], it falls to the RD-2 refund rule unless RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 excuses it [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

The rider's only pre-segment message is Chat #2 at 23:00, "Sure, no problem." [F9], answering the driver's 22:59 question "can I go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road?" [F8]; the chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10], so consent is recorded from the rider herself and not merely claimed by the driver (G11 applied through RD-5). Timing is satisfied: the agreement precedes the 23:03 segment start [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The words, however, are a specific named-road authorisation, not a general "whichever way is faster" choice, so they cover driving on Upper Paya Lebar Road only, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The record does not tie the segment to Upper Paya Lebar Road, and the only locational material is the driver's own post-trip statement that he instead went "by Hougang Avenue 3" [F11][F3]. Both advocates stipulated, and I accept, that on this record the segment is undetermined as to the agreed named road (G13 applied through RD-5) [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5]. That undetermined finding changes the amount (it is the difference between $7.11 payable and nothing), so under RD-5's own terms the case must go to a person rather than be auto-decided [F3][F4][F7][RD-2][RD-5].

No RD-3 stop is in issue: nothing in the chat records a rider-requested stop, and the trace notes no stop measured in this segment [F8][F9][RD-3]. The RD-4 exemption fails: no incident is recorded near the route in the trip window, and the sole congestion record — band 2 on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway 22:40–23:03 — is at most corroborative and cannot exempt on its own [F12][F15][RD-4].

RD-6's additional action does not attach on this record: the driver's profile shows 2 disputes and 1 upheld in 90 days but route disputes upheld = 0 [F18], and the trace marks the RD-6 prior as ✗, so no flag_account [F18][RD-6]. The 2060 m maximum displacement and the 18.7 km vs 13.3 km actual-versus-optimal distance [F1][F3][F16] are noted for the reviewer, as is the metered waiting item of $0.11, which RD-3(c) leaves with the driver [F5][RD-3].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages, the driver's statement and the traffic/weather facts; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F8][F9][F11][F15][F16][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is otherwise complete (GPS, fare, chat, traffic all present); the single element the record does not settle is which road the 23:03–23:14 segment was driven on, which is the reason for escalation [F3][F11][RD-5].
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; evidence unknown: The record does not settle which road the 23:03–23:14 off-route segment was driven on: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path and the only locational material is the driver's post-trip statement naming Hougang Avenue 3 (F3, F11), so the scope of the rider's named-road consent is undetermined (RD-5/G13).

segment_findings.reason: The rider's pre-segment reply 'Sure, no problem.' at 23:00 [F9] answers a driver request limited to a named road, Upper Paya Lebar Road [F8], so consent covers driving on that road only; timing is satisfied (23:00 before the 23:03 start) [F3][F8][F9]. The fact table carries no road name for the driven path, and the driver's own statement says he went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead [F3][F11], so nothing ties the segment to the agreed road and the record leaves the scope undetermined (G13) [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5]. This finding changes the amount, so the case goes to a human.

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted on the timing point (23:00 before the 23:03 start, F3/F8/F9) but rejected as a claim that the segment's ground can be resolved against the driver: with no road-name record tying the segment and the driver's own statement naming a different road (F3, F11), the scope is undetermined under RD-5, and an undetermined segment that changes the amount is referred to a human, not automatically refunded (F3, F4, F7, RD-2, RD-5).

Rejected as a ground for deciding the driver: F11 is a post-trip statement, not rider consent (G11 applied through RD-5), and it is the very record that leaves the segment's scope undetermined rather than proving a refundable deviation; the fare consequence cannot be fixed on this record (F3, F4, F7, F11, RD-2, RD-5).

Rejected: the timing condition is met (F8 22:59, F9 23:00, segment start 23:03 at F3), but with nothing tying the segment to the named road and the driver's statement naming another road, the scope is undetermined under RD-5 rather than settled as uncovered consent (F3, F8, F9, F11, RD-5).

Arithmetic accepted (5.04 km × $1.4102/km = $7.11 against the billed 5.32 km × $1.4102/km = $7.50, F3/F4/F7, RD-2) but the refund cannot execute because the segment's exemption status is undetermined and therefore escalated (F3, F11, RD-5).

Rejected: RD-6 requires a refund greater than zero plus a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, and the trace and profile show route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (F18), so no flag_account attaches and no refund has been fixed (F18, RD-6).

Partially accepted: the record indeed fails to tie the segment to the agreed road (F3, F8, F9, F11, RD-5), but an undetermined finding that changes the amount is not a finding for the driver — the case is escalated, so the driver gains no exemption and the rider gains no automatic refund (F3, F4, F7, RD-2, RD-5).

Rejected as an outer-bound argument: RD-2 refunds the measured unexempt segment's extra_km at this trip's rate, not the billed excess-distance line (F3, F4, F7, RD-2); the $0.11 metered waiting item is correctly excluded under RD-3(c) (F5, RD-3), but no amount can be fixed while the segment is undetermined (F3, F11, RD-5).

Accepted on the RD-6 outcome (no flag_account, F18, RD-6), but rejected insofar as it treats an undetermined segment as a route-dispute finding in the driver's favour; the deviation finding is unresolved and goes to a human (F3, F11, RD-5).
